trial_court: City Civil Court at Calcutta, L.A. No. 15 of 2008
case_name: For The vs Subodh Chandra Kumar
facts_of_case: Anjan passed away intestate; petitioner applied for letters of administration; inventory conducted; subsequent suit filed for declaration and injunction.

legal_principles.principle: A bare possibility of an interest in the estate of the deceased is sufficient to entitle a party to oppose a testamentary paper.
legal_principles.held: In support of his submission that it is not for the testamentary Court to decide whether or not the opposite party is the duly married wife of Anjan and that a bare possibility of an interest in the estate of the deceased would be sufficient to entitle a party to oppose a testamentary paper, reliance was placed by Mr. Banerjee on the Bench decision of this Court reported in AIR 1970 Cal 433 (Sm. Annapurna Kumar v. Subodh Chandra Kumar).
cited_cases: AIR 1970 Cal 433 (Sm. Annapurna Kumar v. Subodh Chandra Kumar)

legal_principles.principle: The law does not require the opposite party to disclose particulars of relatives and their residences.
legal_principles.held: It was further contended that being the brother and only heir of Anjan, he is entitled in law to contest the testamentary paper and the learned Judge ought to have allowed the prayer to contest.

outcome.final_order: The learned Judge's order rejecting the prayer of the petitioner is set aside, and the matter is remanded to the trial court.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for letters of administration
advising on withdrawal of case and suing afresh
assisting in property disputes involving family members
